scope: qualified observed-body retrieval, immutable release and Git publication, proposed interpretation history, automatic v5 catchup
body_delivery: Three real source bodies preserve source, model, rendered structure, notes and column spans.
Every selected fixture is inventoried; rejected documents have no rendered payload.
A pinned lookup returns exact qualified HTML; rejected or absent documents are explicit.
The CLI creates a new HTML file only for a qualified document.
A failed release blocks before any Git data publication.
Real local Git publication binds the exact creation commit and preserves previous materialization receipts.
Published body replay succeeds without reopening the old source or release.
Release transport checks anonymous exact bytes, immutable replay and interrupted draft recovery.
claim_delivery: Proposals bind exact operation revisions and typed evidence locations.
All proposals remain ineligible for legal reconstruction.
Actual local Git publication and supersession preserve original records and creation receipts.
Replay uses checked committed proofs without reopening old evidence releases.
New claims still require full evidence and fail before remote change when it is unavailable.
Missing publication proof, deleted committed history, altered claims and altered receipts are rejected.
catchup: Actual v4/v5 fixture bundles pass the existing intake, pilot, operation and new body stages.
Only v5 produces the new body product; replay preserves accepted receipt bytes.
An induced body-qualification failure retains explicit failed-phase diagnostics and prevents publication.
limits: These checks use small source-bound fixtures and local bare Git remotes; public GitHub delivery remains a separate acceptance step.
Whole-corpus qualification and public bundle readback are not claimed by this report.
This does not establish a legal baseline, commencement interpretation or historical legal state.
